title: Carbon Brake Heat Stack and Wear Pin Standard for Extended Taxi Duty
abstract: A revised heat stack and a re-scaled wear pin for the carbon brake, extending the wear pin datum standard to the airports where long taxi times, rather than landings, are what consumes the stack.

sections.reason: The wear pin datum standard fixed the measurement but not the wear itself, and at four congested airports the operators are seeing stack consumption that the landing count does not explain. Instrumented taxi data from two aircraft shows that between eleven and nineteen per cent of the energy into the stack in a typical day is put there during taxi, at temperatures where the carbon oxidises rather than wearing mechanically. The current stack was optimised for landing energy and behaves poorly in that regime.
sections.description: The heat stack is changed to a carbon grade with an oxidation-inhibited outer disc set, and the wear pin scale is re-marked because the usable stack thickness changes by four millimetres. The brake regulator D3240112571209 introduced by the current standard is retained and only its pin boss is re-drilled to the new scale. The pump kit D3240119570323 is unchanged. Plain washers AGS678120-8C are renewed at the torque tube flange because the assembly is broken. Pump 1GB and the inboard pump 584GB are refitted. Work is at the main gear doors in zone 753 and in the right main gear bay in zone 731. Detail is on drawing D32401123478.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 5.2 kg per brake, twenty-one kilograms per aircraft on the main gear, which is significant enough to be carried in the weight and balance amendment. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable with the current standard and not mixable on a bogie, because the wear scales differ. Stack life at the affected airports is expected to improve by about thirty per cent. The wear check acceptance table is reissued and the brake temperature limitation in the flight crew documentation is restated.
sections.embodiment_note: Design has been launched. Production cut-in is planned once the stack supplier has qualified the outer disc set; retrofit at brake overhaul through a new bulletin. Aircraft must already carry the wear pin datum standard.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis concluded that the change may proceed subject to confirming the weight and balance amendment route, the brake temperature limitation wording, and whether the wear check card can carry two acceptance tables during the transition.

type_data.balance_impact: Aft of the reference datum at the main gear; carried in the amendment
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in planned after stack supplier qualification
